headline: Nashville, Miami, Toronto lead a 29-game swing
dek: Fourteen Eastern matches and fifteen Western contests reshaped the playoff picture across Oct. 14-18.
body: Nashville SC hammered Sporting Kansas City 4-0 at home and drew 1-1 at San Jose to close the week. Inter Miami beat Atlanta United twice, 2-0 and 3-1, with New York City FC on the wrong end of a 2-0 loss at Miami before holding LAFC to a 1-1 draw. Toronto FC drew 3-3 at home with Orlando then won 2-0 at Red Bull New York. Philadelphia Union dropped 1-3 at Chicago before drawing 2-2 with Charlotte. LA Galaxy beat Portland 2-0 and drew 2-2 with San Diego. LAFC defeated Austin 3-1. Portland and Colorado played to a 0-0 draw, as did St. Louis and Vancouver.

headline: Herrington exits Colorado for Hull City
dek: The 18-year-old defender logged 1,650 minutes for the Rapids before a Premier League move ended his MLS stint.
body: Colorado Rapids defender Lucas Herrington has transferred to Hull City of the English Premier League, the club confirmed in August. Herrington accumulated 1,650 minutes for Colorado this season before departing. The deal represents the largest transfer fee the Rapids have ever received and the highest fee for any defender in MLS history. Colorado retains a percentage of future sell-on rights.

headline: Musa holds a one-goal lead at the top
dek: FC Dallas striker Petar Musa sits on 20 goals with Milan Iloski and Rafael Navarro close behind.
body: Petar Musa of FC Dallas leads the scoring race with 20 goals. Philadelphia Union's Milan Iloski is one back at 19, while St. Louis CITY SC's Rafael Navarro sits third with 18. In assists, San Diego FC's Anders Dreyer leads at 12. Nashville SC's Cristian Espinoza and Seattle's Albert Rusnák are tied at 11. On the tackle charts, Vancouver's Andrés Cubas dominates at 109, with Inter Miami's Yannick Bright second at 77 and D.C. United's Silvan Hefti third at 76.

headline: Nashville's defense makes the East a one-horse race
dek: The Eastern leader holds a 67-point total with the league's stingiest back line; the West remains tightly contested.
body: Nashville SC lead the Eastern Conference with 67 points on a 20W-7D-3L record, having conceded only 23 goals, the best defensive mark in the league. Their attack has produced 64 goals. In the West, Vancouver Whitecaps top the table at 55 points, 16W-7D-7L. Inter Miami CF carry the league's sharpest attack at 73 goals for the season. In the xG tables, Houston's Guilherme leads overperformers at plus-8.9 (16 goals, 7.1 xG), while Chicago's Philip Zinckernagel is the biggest underperformer at minus-5.0 (6 goals, 11.0 xG).

headline: St. Louis routs Galaxy 6-2; Nashville blanks SKC 4-0
dek: A 16-game stretch spanning Oct. 11-15 produced 47 goals, three scoreless draws, and one nine-goal thriller.
body: St. Louis CITY SC put six past LA Galaxy on Oct. 11 before drawing 0-0 with Vancouver two days later. Nashville SC hammered Sporting Kansas City 4-0 at home. Atlanta United won 3-0 at CF Montréal, Columbus beat Charlotte 3-1, and D.C. United edged Red Bull New York 2-1. New England stunned FC Cincinnati 3-2 on the road. Inter Miami shut out NYCFC 2-0. Toronto and Orlando shared a 3-3 draw. Philadelphia took three points at Chicago Fire 3-1, and LAFC defeated Austin FC 3-1. FC Dallas beat Seattle 1-0. San Diego and Houston traded goals in a 3-3 draw, Colorado and Minnesota finished 2-2, Real Salt Lake and San Jose drew 1-1, and LA Galaxy rebounded to beat Portland 2-0.

headline: Martínez to Midtjylland, Bombino to Stoke City
dek: Two young players exit MLS mid-season, each logging 1,290 minutes before departing for Europe.
body: LAFC transferred forward David Martínez to FC Midtjylland of the Danish Superliga, with both clubs confirming the move. Martínez logged 1,290 minutes for LAFC this season. San Diego FC transferred defender Luca Bombino to EFL Championship side Stoke City on a permanent deal, also confirmed by both clubs. Bombino, who spent two seasons with San Diego after initially joining on loan from LAFC, also had 1,290 minutes on the field in 2026 before departing.

headline: Musa leads at 19; Iloski and Denkey give chase
dek: Three strikers are separated by two goals with the regular season drawing to a close.
body: FC Dallas forward Petar Musa sits atop the scoring charts with 19 goals. Philadelphia Union's Milan Iloski is one back at 18, and FC Cincinnati's Kévin Denkey trails by two at 17. In the assists race, San Diego FC's Anders Dreyer leads with 12. Nashville SC's Cristian Espinoza and Seattle Sounders' Albert Rusnák are tied at 11. Andrés Cubas of Vancouver Whitecaps dominates the tackles table with 106, well ahead of Inter Miami's Yannick Bright at 77 and D.C. United's Silvan Hefti at 74.

headline: Nashville dominant East; Vancouver lead the West
dek: Nashville's defensive numbers are historically tight as both conferences enter the final stretch.
body: Nashville SC lead the Eastern Conference with 66 points on a 20W-6D-3L record, having conceded only 22 goals, the best defensive mark in the league, while scoring 63. Vancouver Whitecaps top the West at 52 points, 15W-7D-7L, with 61 goals scored and 30 conceded. Inter Miami CF carry the league's most potent attack with 70 goals scored. Nashville's 22 goals allowed stands alone as the stingiest defensive record across both conferences.

headline: St. Louis rolls Galaxy 6-2; Miami, Nashville keep rolling
dek: A chaotic midweek double-header produced 30 games, two routs, and no shortage of dropped points at the bottom.
body: St. Louis CITY SC hammered LA Galaxy 6-2 on Oct. 11 in the week's most lopsided result. Inter Miami posted back-to-back shutouts, beating D.C. United 4-0 and New York City FC 2-0. Nashville SC handed Austin FC a 4-1 defeat then crushed Sporting Kansas City 4-0 four days later. Red Bull New York routed San Diego FC 4-1. FC Cincinnati rallied to win 3-1 at Atlanta before falling 2-3 at home to New England. Seven of the 30 fixtures ended level, including a 3-3 draw at Sporting Kansas City and a 6-goal share in Portland's visit to Kansas City.

headline: Houston lose two; Columbus, Toronto add from within
dek: The Dynamo's summer clearout is now confirmed, with both departures landing at clubs outside MLS.
body: Defender Erik Sviatchenko, 1,530 minutes for Houston Dynamo this season, has signed with Thai top-flight side Port FC after the clubs mutually terminated his contract. Midfielder Jack McGlynn, 1,500 minutes this season, was transferred to EFL Championship side Stoke City. On the arrivals side, Columbus Crew promoted forward Kevin Gbamblé from Crew 2 on a first-team contract through June 2029, after he posted 23 goal contributions in 27 MLS NEXT Pro matches this year. Toronto FC signed homegrown midfielder Antone Bossenberry Romero, 18, to a deal through the 2028-29 season after 33 appearances for TFC II.

headline: Musa leads Golden Boot at 19; Dreyer tops assists
dek: The scoring and chance-creation races tighten as the regular season approaches its final weekend.
body: Petar Musa of FC Dallas leads the Golden Boot race with 19 goals. Philadelphia Union's Milan Iloski sits one back at 18, with FC Cincinnati's Kévin Denkey third at 17. In assists, San Diego FC's Anders Dreyer holds the lead at 12, one clear of Nashville SC's Cristian Espinoza and Seattle's Albert Rusnák, who are level at 11. Vancouver's Andrés Cubas dominates the tackles chart at 106, well ahead of Inter Miami's Yannick Bright at 77 and D.C. United's Silvan Hefti at 74.

headline: Nashville's defense defines the East; Vancouver leads the West
dek: Nashville's goal differential alone tells most of the story at the top of the standings.
body: Nashville SC lead the Eastern Conference on 66 points, a 20W-6D-3L record with 63 goals for and just 22 against, the best defensive mark in the league. Inter Miami hold the best attack in MLS at 70 goals. In the West, Vancouver Whitecaps sit top on 52 points at 15W-7D-7L, having conceded 30 against 61 scored. Houston Dynamo's McGlynn and Sviatchenko departures could test the depth of a club pushing for a playoff place with the table set for a final-round crunch.
